prompt:

Reply with ONLY one JSON object:

   "gardner": David Gardner: Rule Breaker Investing (The six Rule Breaker traits (Motley Fool Rule Breakers; “Rule Breakers, Rule Makers”, 1998))

 "checklist": { "<id>": {"verdict": "yes|partly|no|unknown", "evidence": "one specific sentence"} } for EVERY id below (each question is shared by the frameworks that ask it):
   "momentum": Has the share price risen strongly over roughly the last six to twelve months, beating the market?
   "g4": Is it run by great leaders and backed by smart, well-known investors or partners?

   "integrity": Is management honest and candid with shareholders, rational with capital, paid in a way that lines up with owners, and well governed?

   "roic": Does it earn a high, consistent return on the capital it uses, without relying on debt?

   "fairprice": Is the price reasonable for the quality and growth on offer?
   "mu5": Thinking backwards, are there few ways this business could fail?
   "reinvest": Can it reinvest its profits at high returns for many years?

   "ly3": Is the price/earnings ratio at or below the earnings growth rate?

   "ly7": Are insiders buying and is the company reducing its share count?
   "ly8": Is it overlooked by Wall Street or in a 'boring' niche?
   "fi2": Is management committed to developing new products as current ones mature?
   "fi3": Does its R&D spending produce results?
   "fi4": Is it unusually good at selling?
   "longterm": Does management put long-term value and innovation ahead of short-term profit?
   "gr1": Is it a large, established company?
   "ni10": Has it been profitable in each of the last ten years?
   "gr4": Has it paid a dividend every year for at least 20 years?
   "eps10": Has earnings per share grown by at least one third over ten years?
   "gr6": Is the share price no more than about 15 times average earnings?
   "gr7": Is price/earnings × price/book no more than about 22.5?
   "th1": Does it have proprietary technology about ten times better than the next best?
   "timing": Is the technology and market timing right for this business now?
   "th3": Did it start with a big share of a small market, and can it expand from there?
   "team": Is it led by an exceptional founder or world-class management team?
   "th5": Does it have a way to reach and sell to customers, not just a product?
   "durable": Will its market position still hold in 10 to 20 years, resisting disruption and obsolescence?
   "th7": Has it found a unique opportunity that others don't see?
   "trend": Is it a leading beneficiary of a major platform shift or secular trend (such as AI or cloud computing)?
   "dr1": Are earnings accelerating and analysts' estimates moving up?
   "dr2": Will the business look better in 18–24 months than today, beyond what is already obvious?
   "dr4": Do interest rates, central-bank liquidity and the economy work in its favour?

   "dr7": Is conviction high enough that it could be a large, concentrated position?

   "pa2": Is the business or industry going through a temporary, fixable setback?
   "pa4": Is the chance of permanent loss small even if the outcome is uncertain?
   "wo1": Is it a leader in AI, robotics, energy storage, blockchain or multiomic sequencing?
   "wo2": Are its product costs falling quickly as volumes grow, opening up big new demand?
   "wo3": Does it combine several innovation platforms?
   "wo4": Could its addressable market be many times larger in five years?
   "ac3": Is it largely insulated from commodity prices, interest rates and similar outside forces?
   "ns1": Does it pass the savings from its growing size back to customers, making it ever harder to compete with?
   "ns4": Is its likely position in 10–20 years clearly stronger than today?
   "va2": Does the product solve a large, painful problem?
   "tn1": Does it sell into a real secular trend (like AI, energy or robotics; ideally the infrastructure layer), as a company built for that trend rather than an old business retrofitting?
   "tn2": Is there a gap between the story the market tells about the company and what it is actually becoming (like Palantir seen as a consultancy, Tesla as a car company)?
   "tn3": Is it outside the zones to avoid: small caps, Chinese companies, commodity producers, airlines, seasonal businesses and startups?
   "tn4": Of these three, does it pass at least two (and have a valid reason for any miss, such as infrastructure needing leverage or a clear path to profit): revenue grown for the past few years, profitable, more cash than debt?
   "tn5": Has free cash flow been positive, and cash exceeded debt, in each of the last 4 to 6 quarters?
   "tn6": Is revenue growing at 10% a year or more?
   "tn7": Is revenue growth % plus free-cash-flow margin % at least 40?
   "tn8": Over the last year, did revenue grow faster than total operating expenses?
   "tn9": Does it avoid every instant kill: market cap under $1B, more debt than cash, short interest above 10%, operating margin below 20%, revenue growth below 10% and falling, two or more earnings misses in the last 4 quarters, or less than 10 years since founding?
   "tn10": Is it free of any major regulatory or legal threat?
   "tn11": Can it be stated plainly as “provides X that helps Y achieve Z, and charges [revenue model]”, with a clear answer to what pain it cures, who is in pain, and why customers choose it over competitors?
   "tn13": Score it on Nash's 13 categories, 0, 5 or 10 each, using the last twelve months: cash vs debt (more debt / more cash / 2x+ cash), revenue growth (<10% / 10-20% / >20%), operating margin (<10% / 10-25% / >25%), short interest (>10% / 5-10% / <5%), institutional ownership (<30% / 30-60% / >60%), revenue growing faster than expenses (no 0 / yes 10), 5-year return vs the S&P 500 (behind / ahead by 10-20% / ahead by 20%+), and, judged harshly, moat, CEO, recession-proof pricing power, secular trend, culture and mission, talent (none / some / strong). Is the total 75 or more? Give the total in the evidence.
   "tn14": Over the last five years, has revenue grown every year, operating margin expanded, free cash flow been positive and rising, and cash exceeded debt every year?
   "tn15": Would a banker lend to it: interest coverage (operating income ÷ interest) of 4x or more, assets (excluding goodwill) at least 2× liabilities, current ratio of 1 or more, and total liabilities under 4× equity?
   "tn18": Does the CEO have a track record of execution (growth, margins, innovation), skin in the game through open-market share purchases, and 10+ years in the role, ideally as founder?
   "tn20": Has it consistently beaten earnings expectations?
   "tn21": Is it free of every red flag: a clown CEO, a co-CEO structure, an acquisition spree, any suspicion of fraud or accounting problems, an auditor change, declining margins, revenue spiking while inventory piles up, or insiders selling hard while the stock runs?
   "tn22": Does it avoid the hype trap of no revenue, weak fundamentals, constant share sales to raise cash and nonstop media hype?
   "tn24": Working back from today's price, is the growth the price implies below what the company is already delivering?
   "tn25": With Nash's DCF (3-year averages of revenue growth and FCF margin, trimmed growth, 5 years of free cash flow, 4% terminal growth, plus cash minus debt), is the value per share above today's price even at a 12% discount rate?
   "tn26": Using the multiple that fits (forward P/E vs peers for mature companies, hardware and banks; Rule of 40 for software; price to sales vs the industry for unprofitable growth), is it attractive, with a PEG (forward P/E ÷ EPS growth) of 1 or less?

summaries.gardner: Robinhood has several Rule Breaker traits: a founder-led, fast-innovating company with a well-known brand, riding mobile investing, crypto and prediction markets, and often called overvalued. But it is not the clear leader of an emerging industry, its moat is modest, and the shares fell about 34% over the past year, so the fit is partial but meaningful.
summaries.buffett: Robinhood is now very profitable (a 42% net margin on $4,473M of 2025 revenue), but its earnings depend on volatile retail trading and interest rates, it only became profitable in 2024, and it has a short, uneven record. At about 46 times 2025 earnings it offers no margin of safety, so it fits Buffett's approach poorly.
summaries.munger: Munger valued durable moats, simple predictable businesses and trustworthy management, and was openly critical of Robinhood's gamified trading and payment-for-order-flow model. Its reliance on options, crypto and event-contract trading makes it a poor fit for his approach.
summaries.lynch: Robinhood is a clear fast grower that ordinary investors understand (revenue up 52% in 2025), but its P/E of about 46 is far above its sustainable growth rate (consensus about 19% revenue growth in 2026), and its earnings are cyclical with markets. Lynch would like the story but probably not the price or the cyclicality.
summaries.fisher: Robinhood fits several Fisher points: a strong pipeline of new products (banking, prediction markets, tokenization, Cortex AI), sales growth well above peers and expanding margins. Weaker points are its regulatory history, low switching costs and uneven customer trust.
summaries.graham: Robinhood fails Graham's defensive criteria: it has been profitable only since 2024, pays no dividend, trades at about 46 times 2025 earnings and over 9 times book value. It does not suit a defensive investor.
summaries.thiel: Robinhood started as a near-monopoly on free mobile trading for young investors, and still leads in some new niches like retail event contracts and tokenized stocks, but its technology is not 10x better than rivals now that $0 commissions are universal. It answers Thiel's distribution and team questions well, but durability and monopoly questions less well.
summaries.gerstner: Robinhood has the growth, margin expansion and founder-led execution Gerstner looks for, plus a clear product cycle (banking, prediction markets, international). But a P/E near 46, a 34% share-price fall over the past year and dependence on volatile trading revenue make the risk-reward less clear-cut.
summaries.druckenmiller: Robinhood is a high-beta liquidity play: it thrives when retail risk appetite, crypto prices and markets are strong, and its earnings reaccelerated in Q2 2026 (EPS $0.62, up 48%). Weak price momentum (down about 34% over the year) and a crypto slowdown mean the setup is mixed rather than compelling.
summaries.smith: Terry Smith wants high, consistent returns on capital and resilient, predictable businesses; Robinhood's returns are new and swing with trading volumes, and free cash flow is volatile quarter to quarter. Its valuation is also not cheap, so it fits Fundsmith's approach poorly.
summaries.greenblatt: Robinhood has a high recent return on equity (about 22% in 2025) but a low earnings yield at about 46 times earnings, and as a broker its returns on capital are hard to compare. It would not rank well on the Magic Formula.
summaries.akre: Akre's stool needs a great business, talented owner-minded management and reinvestment opportunities. Robinhood scores well on founder management and reinvestment runway, but the business quality (low switching costs, volatile revenue, regulatory exposure) is weaker than Akre's typical compounders.
summaries.pabrai: Pabrai looks for simple, low-risk businesses at deep discounts with heads-I-win odds; Robinhood is a high-beta growth stock at a premium valuation with regulatory and cyclical risks. It does not fit the Dhandho approach.
summaries.wood: Robinhood fits ARK's themes of blockchain, tokenization and digital wallets, and ARK has long held the stock. It is pushing tokenized stocks, its own Robinhood Chain and AI tools, making it one of the more innovation-driven financial firms, though most revenue still comes from conventional trading and interest.
summaries.ackman: Ackman seeks simple, predictable, free-cash-flow-generative businesses with strong moats; Robinhood is profitable but its cash flows are volatile and depend on markets and rates, and its moat is moderate. It fits his criteria only partly.
summaries.sleep: Nick Sleep's scale-economics-shared model fits Robinhood's original idea of passing savings to customers through $0 commissions and high interest on cash for Gold members. But its revenue still leans on payment for order flow and trading activity rather than the patient, ever-cheaper model of Costco or Amazon, so the fit is partial.
summaries.valentine: Valentine looked for huge markets and a product that solves a big problem; Robinhood's early $0-commission mobile app did that for young investors and reshaped the industry. Today its market is huge but crowded, so it is less of a classic Sequoia-style opportunity than it was at founding.
summaries.nash: Robinhood scores well on Nash's numbers (revenue growth above 20%, 47% pre-tax margin, more cash than debt, revenue growing faster than costs) and is founder-led. It misses on free-cash-flow consistency, valuation (the DCF value is well below the price) and regulatory risk around payment for order flow and prediction markets.

momentum.evidence: HOOD fell about 33.6% over the 52 weeks to late October 2026 (StockAnalysis), while the S&P 500 (SPY) returned about 14.6%.

g4.evidence: Founder-CEO Vlad Tenev leads the company, which was backed early by Index Ventures, Ribbit Capital and Andreessen Horowitz, and Robinhood joined the S&P 500 in September 2025.

g6.evidence: At about 46 times 2025 earnings ($95.07 vs $2.05 diluted EPS) and a PEG of about 1.8, many commentators call HOOD expensive compared with Schwab and Interactive Brokers.

simple.evidence: A trading app earning from trades, interest and subscriptions is easy to grasp, but payment for order flow, crypto, event contracts and broker balance-sheet cash flows make results harder to predict.

b2.evidence: Robinhood lost money every year from 2021 to 2023 (a $541M net loss in 2023) and revenue fell 25% in 2022, so it has only two years of profits.

integrity.evidence: Management buys back stock ($653M in 2025) and communicates openly, but Class B super-voting shares give founders control, insiders are regular sellers, and the firm has paid large regulatory fines (including $29.75M to FINRA in March 2025).

b6.evidence: Robinhood mostly builds new products itself, but it has made a string of acquisitions (Bitstamp, TradePMR, WonderFi, an Indonesian broker) and expanded into many adjacent lines quickly.

roic.evidence: Return on equity was about 22% in 2025 ($1,883M net income on average equity of about $8.6B), but this is recent, and StockAnalysis puts ROIC at about 7% because of its broker balance sheet.

fcf.evidence: Free cash flow was about $1,584M in 2025 (operating cash flow $1,638M less $54M capital spending), close to net income of $1,883M, but it swings widely by quarter (TTM to June 2026 only about $219M) because of customer-related balances.

b10.evidence: Equity rose from $7,972M to $9,151M in 2025 while market value grew far more since the 2021 IPO at $38, but the company only recently began earning profits to retain.

safety.evidence: At $95.07 the shares trade at about 46 times 2025 earnings and over 9 times book value, and a conservative DCF gives a value well below the price.

fairprice.evidence: A P/E near 46 and forward P/E near 36 are high for a broker, though partly justified by 52% revenue growth in 2025 and 32% in Q2 2026.

mu5.evidence: It could be hurt by a ban on payment for order flow, a crackdown on sports event contracts, a crypto bear market, falling rates or a reputational crisis like GameStop in 2021.

reinvest.evidence: Robinhood keeps launching high-return lines (13 business lines above $100M annualized revenue by Q2 2026) with modest capital spending of $54M in 2025.

ly2.evidence: It is a fast grower: revenue rose from $1,865M in 2023 to $4,473M in 2025 as it adds customers, assets and products.

ly3.evidence: Its P/E of about 46 is far above expected growth (consensus revenue growth of about 19% for 2026 and a StockAnalysis PEG of about 1.8).

runway.evidence: It is expanding into banking, retirement, advisor custody, international markets (over 1 million international funded customers by mid-2026) and tokenized assets.

ly7.evidence: The company is buying back stock ($653M in 2025 and $414M in Q2 2026) and diluted shares fell from 918.8M in 2025 to 912M in Q2 2026, but insiders such as co-founder Baiju Bhatt are regular sellers.

ly8.evidence: Robinhood is a heavily covered S&P 500 stock with about 68.5% institutional ownership and constant media attention.

fi2.evidence: It launched prediction markets, Robinhood Banking, short selling, Robinhood Chain, the Rothera exchange and the Cortex AI assistant in 2025-2026.

fi3.evidence: Technology and development spending of $897M in 2025 helped produce new lines such as event contracts, which earned $156M in Q2 2026 alone.

fi4.evidence: Robinhood gathered $68B of net deposits in 2025 and $21.7B in Q2 2026, with Gold subscribers up 39% to 4.8 million, showing strong marketing and product-led selling.

longterm.evidence: Founder control lets it invest in long-term bets such as tokenization, Robinhood Chain and international expansion while keeping cost growth below revenue growth.

gr1.evidence: It is an S&P 500 member with a market value of roughly $85B and $4,473M of 2025 revenue.

ni10.evidence: Robinhood lost money in 2021, 2022 and 2023 and was profitable only in 2024 and 2025.

eps10.evidence: It has been public only since July 2021 and had losses until 2024, so there is no 10-year record of EPS growth.

gr6.evidence: The price is about 46 times 2025 diluted EPS of $2.05, far above 15 times average earnings.

gr7.evidence: P/E of about 46 times price/book of about 9.5 gives roughly 440, far above 22.5.

th1.evidence: Its app is well designed, but rivals offer $0 commissions and similar features, so its technology is not 10 times better.

timing.evidence: Mobile investing, tokenization and regulated prediction markets are all growing now, and Robinhood launched products like Rothera (June 2026) early.

th3.evidence: It started by dominating free mobile trading for young investors and has since expanded into retirement, banking, crypto and event contracts.

team.evidence: Founder-CEO Vlad Tenev has led a turnaround from a $541M loss in 2023 to $1,883M of net income in 2025.

th5.evidence: Its consumer brand and referral and Gold incentives bring in customers directly: funded customers reached 28.4 million in June 2026.

durable.evidence: Its brand and product pace are strong, but low switching costs, regulatory risk to payment for order flow and new rivals make its position in 10 to 20 years uncertain.

th7.evidence: It saw early that young investors wanted free mobile trading and now prediction markets and tokenized stocks, but rivals quickly copied $0 commissions.

trend.evidence: It benefits from mobile-first investing, crypto, tokenization and prediction markets, and from the transfer of wealth to younger generations.

dr1.evidence: Q2 2026 EPS of $0.62 rose 48% and beat the $0.43 consensus, but Q1 2026 missed on revenue and EPS and crypto revenue fell 38%.

dr2.evidence: Banking, international and event contracts could make it bigger and more diversified in 18-24 months, but a lot of growth is already expected and trading activity is cyclical.

dr4.evidence: Strong markets and liquidity boost trading, but falling interest rates would reduce net interest revenue, which was 34% of 2025 revenue.

dr6.evidence: Catalysts include the Rothera exchange ramp, Robinhood Banking roll-out, UK crypto and Singapore launches and Q3 2026 results on October 27, 2026.

dr7.evidence: With a beta of about 2.35, regulatory risks and volatile earnings, it is hard to justify a large concentrated position.

gm.evidence: Robinhood does not report a gross margin; brokerage and transaction costs were only $211M on $4,473M revenue in 2025, but its $0-commission pricing shows limited pricing power.

fcfyield.evidence: TTM free cash flow of about $219M gives a yield of about 0.3% (StockAnalysis); even 2025's roughly $1,584M is under 2% of an ~$85B market value.

gb2.evidence: 2025 pre-tax income of $2,108M is only about 2.5% of an enterprise value of roughly $82B.

pa2.evidence: The share price fell about 34% over the past year as crypto trading cooled, a cyclical setback rather than a broken business.

pa4.evidence: It has more corporate cash than debt and is profitable, but its high valuation means a real risk of permanent loss if growth slows.

wo1.evidence: It is a blockchain leader among brokers through Bitstamp, tokenized stocks in Europe and the Robinhood Chain Ethereum layer-2 mainnet launched in 2026.

wo2.evidence: Its scale lets it offer $0 commissions and cheaper crypto and event contracts, but its cost decline is not as dramatic as in batteries or sequencing.

wo3.evidence: It combines blockchain/tokenization, AI (Cortex assistant) and digital wallets, though mainly as a user rather than an inventor of these platforms.

wo4.evidence: Tokenization and global expansion could greatly widen its market, but a many-fold increase in five years is uncertain.

ac3.evidence: Its results depend heavily on interest rates (net interest was 34% of 2025 revenue) and crypto prices (crypto was 20%).

ns1.evidence: It passes scale savings to customers through $0 commissions, high cash yields and IRA matches for Gold members, but still relies on payment for order flow.

ns4.evidence: Its product breadth and assets are growing fast ($369B platform assets in June 2026), but its long-term position against Schwab, Fidelity and crypto exchanges is not clearly assured.

va2.evidence: It made investing cheap and accessible for millions, though the problem of costly trading has largely been solved industry-wide.

tn1.evidence: It is a company built for mobile, crypto and tokenized finance, but not an infrastructure layer of a trend like AI or energy.

tn2.evidence: The market often sees a meme-stock trading app, while it is becoming a broad financial platform with banking, retirement, an exchange and a blockchain.

tn3.evidence: It is a large-cap US company outside commodity, airline, seasonal and startup zones.

tn4.evidence: Revenue grew each of the last three years (to $4,473M in 2025), it is profitable, and corporate cash of about $5.4B exceeds about $2.2B of debt.

tn5.evidence: Corporate cash has exceeded debt, but free cash flow was negative in Q3 2025 (about -$1,579M) and Q4 2025 (about -$939M) per StockAnalysis.

tn6.evidence: Revenue grew 52% in 2025 and 32% in Q2 2026.

tn7.evidence: 2025 revenue growth of 52% plus a free-cash-flow margin of about 35% is well above 40.

tn8.evidence: In 2025 revenue grew 52% while total operating expenses grew 25%.

tn9.evidence: Market cap is about $85B, cash exceeds debt, short interest is about 5.1%, pre-tax margin is 47%, growth is above 10%, only one EPS miss (Q1 2026) in the last four quarters, and it was founded in 2013.

tn10.evidence: It faces state challenges to sports event contracts (e.g. Massachusetts), possible payment-for-order-flow rules and a history of regulatory fines.

tn11.evidence: Robinhood provides a low-cost investing and trading app that helps everyday people invest and trade stocks, options, crypto and event contracts, charging through order-flow payments, spreads, interest and Gold subscriptions.

tn13.evidence: Total about 90: cash vs debt 10, revenue growth 10, operating margin 10, short interest 5, institutional ownership 10, revenue faster than expenses 10, 5-year return vs S&P 500 10 (about +150% since the $38 July 2021 IPO vs roughly +75% for the S&P 500, not exactly 5 years), moat 5, CEO 5, pricing power 0, secular trend 5, culture and mission 5, talent 5.

tn14.evidence: Revenue fell in 2022 and free cash flow was negative in 2024 (operating cash flow -$157M).

tn15.evidence: Interest coverage is very high and liabilities were 3.2 times equity at end-2025, but assets excluding goodwill ($37.8B) were only 1.3 times liabilities ($29.0B), typical of a broker.

tn18.evidence: Founder Vlad Tenev has run the company since 2013 (sole CEO since 2020) with strong growth and innovation, but there is no record of open-market share purchases.

tn20.evidence: It beat EPS estimates for four straight quarters before missing in Q1 2026 ($0.38 vs $0.39), then beat strongly in Q2 2026 ($0.62 vs $0.43).

tn21.evidence: No co-CEO or accounting concerns today, but insiders sell regularly, it has made several acquisitions (Bitstamp, TradePMR, WonderFi) and had a CFO transition in 2026.

tn22.evidence: It has real revenue ($4,473M in 2025), strong profits and is buying back shares rather than issuing them.

tn24.evidence: At $95.07 a reverse DCF (12% discount, 30% FCF margin) implies about 47% annual revenue growth for five years, above the 32% delivered in Q2 2026 and the roughly 19% consensus for 2026.

tn25.evidence: Using trimmed 25% growth and a 30% FCF margin (3-year average), a 12% discount rate and 4% terminal growth plus about $3.2B net cash gives about $47 a share, below $95.07.

tn26.evidence: Forward P/E of about 36 is well above Schwab and Interactive Brokers, and the PEG is about 1.8.
